details.description: Generative is Amazon Polly's largest text-to-speech engine to date, built on a billion-parameter transformer that converts text into speech codes plus a convolution-based decoder that renders them into waveforms in a streamable way. Amazon describes it as producing the most human-like, emotionally engaged, and adaptive conversational voices available in Polly, aimed at uses such as a customer assistant, a virtual trainer, or an advertiser voice. Polly currently offers 43 Generative voices across languages including English, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, and Spanish.
advantages: Amazon calls it the largest Polly TTS model to date, describing its voices as the most human-like, emotionally engaged, and adaptive conversational voices in Polly.
Supports Amazon Polly's Bidirectional Streaming API for simultaneous streaming input and output, in a subset of AWS regions.
Offers 43 voices across 23 language and locale variants, including English, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, and Spanish.
Supports both real-time and asynchronous speech synthesis, and MP3, OGG (Vorbis), and raw PCM output formats.
disadvantages: Does not support the Newscaster speaking style, which is available for some other Polly voices.
Does not currently support generating speech marks.

Amazon warns that updates to the model's training data can cause slight variations in how a voice sounds over time, which can affect projects synthesized in parts over a long period, such as a season of podcasts.
Amazon notes a built-in emergency-stop mechanism reduces but does not eliminate the risk of the model hallucinating or cutting off a word mid-generation.
use_cases: Applications needing simultaneous streaming input and output via the Bidirectional Streaming API

sources.title: Applying the newscaster voice - Amazon Polly

notes: No accuracy-style benchmark scores for the Generative engine were found on Amazon's pages, so evaluations is left empty. Region and voice availability differ by AWS region (e.g. only a subset of voices are offered in Europe (London), Canada (Central) and Europe (Zurich)); not restated here since it is a Bud routing/hosting detail.
